en: A stone milepost (or by extension in other materials), one of a series of numbered markers placed along a road at regular intervals, typi…
An important event in a person's life or career, in the history of a nation, in the life of some project, etc.
To place milestones along (a road, etc.).
To plan out a project as a series of major steps.

milestone.ety: From mile + stone. Compare Dutch mijlsteen (“milestone”), German Low German Mielensteen (“milestone”), German Meilenstein (“milestone”), Swedish milsten (“milestone”).

note.ja: mile（マイル）+ stone（石）。「1マイルごとに置いた石」→「里程標」→「節目・画期的な出来事」。

en: A large cup for beverages, usually having a handle and used without a saucer.
To assault for the purpose of robbery.
To exaggerate a facial expression for communicative emphasis; to make a face, to pose, as for photographs or in a performance, in an exag…

mug.ety: Early 16th century (originally Scots and northern English, denoting "earthenware, pot, jug"), of unknown origin, perhaps from North Germanic (compare Swedish mugg (“mug, jug”), Norwegian mugge (“pitcher, open can for warm drinks”), Danish mugge), or Low German mokke, mukke (“mug”), German Low German Muck (“drinking cup”), Dutch mok (“mug”), also of unknown origin. Perhaps related to Old English muga (“stack”) and Old Norse múgr (“mass, heap (of corn)”). Compare also Middle English mug, mog (“a measure of salt”).

ex.en: Have you ever been mugged?
ex.ja: 強盗に遭ったことがありますか。

ex.en: Hand me my mug.
ex.ja: 私のマグカップ取って。

ex.en: Who broke the mug?
ex.ja: 誰がマグ割ったの？

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。「取っ手付きのカップ」→ 顔（俗）→ 顔を狙って襲う →「強盗する」。

en: A district with a government that typically encloses no other governed districts; a borough, city, or incorporated town or village.
The governing body of such a district.

municipality.ety: Borrowed from French municipalité (Edmund Burke), from municipal + -ité, from Latin municipalis, from municipium (“free city, township”), from municeps (“citizen of a free city or township”), from mūnus (“duty, service”) + -ceps (“taker, catcher”). Equivalent to municipal + -ity.

en: Any of the fleshy fruiting bodies of fungi typically produced above ground on soil or on their food sources (such as decaying wood).
A fungus producing such fruiting bodies.
Having characteristics like those of a mushroom, for example in shape or appearance, speed of growth, or texture.
To grow quickly to a large size or rapidly increase in scope or scale.
To gather mushrooms.

mushroom.ety: From Middle English muscheron, musseron, from Anglo-Norman musherum, moscheron, from Old French moisseron, of obscure origin: probably derived from Old French mosse, moise ("moss"; whence also French mousse), as the use first applied to a type of fungus which grows in moss, from Frankish *mosu (“moss”) or Old Dutch *mosa (“moss”), akin to Old High German mosa (“moor, swamp”), Old High German mos (“moss, bog”), Old High German mios (“moss, mire”), Old English mēos (“moss”), Old English mōs (“bog, marsh”), Old Norse mosi (“moss”), Old Norse myrr (“bog, mire”), from Proto-Germanic *musą, *musô, *

ex.ja: 木の下にいくつかの野生のキノコを見つけた。

ex.ja: 木におびただしいほどのキノコがなっている。

ex.en: This mushroom is not good to eat.

en: A cell of the nervous system, which conducts nerve impulses; consisting of an axon and several dendrites. Neurons are connected by synapses.
A nervure of an insect's wing.

neuron.ety: From New Latin, from Ancient Greek νεῦρον (neûron, “nerve”), doublet of nerve and sinew. By surface analysis, neuro- + -on.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 neuron（腱・神経）から。「神経細胞」。neurology、neural と同じ。

en: The cardinal number occurring after eighty-nine and before ninety-one, represented in Roman numerals as XC and in Arabic numerals as 90.

ninety.ety: From Middle English nynty, nynety, from Old English hundniġontiġ, from Proto-Germanic *newuntēhundą (“ninety”), equivalent to nine + -ty. Cognate with Scots nynty, nynety (“ninety”), Saterland Frisian njuugentich (“ninety”), West Frisian njoggentich (“ninety”), Dutch negentig (“ninety”), German Low German negentig (“ninety”), German neunzig (“ninety”), Swedish nittio (“ninety”), Norwegian Bokmål nitti (“ninety”), Norwegian Nynorsk nitti (“ninety”), Icelandic níutíu (“ninety”).

ex.en: He is likely to live to be ninety.
ex.ja: 彼は９０歳まで生きそうだ。

ex.en: An hour and a half is ninety minutes.
ex.ja: 1時間半は90分です。

ex.en: Few people live to be ninety years old.
ex.ja: ９０歳まで生きる人は少ない。

en: A source of nourishment, such as food, that can be metabolized by an organism to give energy and build tissue.
Providing nourishment.

nutrient.ety: Borrowed from Latin nūtriēns, present participle of nūtriō (“to suckle, nourish, foster”).

ex.en: The avocado is rich in nutrients.
ex.ja: アボカドは栄養豊富です。

note.ja: ラテン語 nutrire（養う）から。「栄養素」。nutrition、nurse と同じ。

en: A place where stars, planets and other celestial bodies are observed, usually through a telescope; also place for observing meteorologica…
A lookout (vantage point with a view of the surrounding area)

observatory.ety: Borrowed from French observatoire, equivalent to observe + -atory.

ex.ja: その天文台はよい位置にある。

note.ja: observe（観測する）+ -atory（場所）。「観測所・天文台」。laboratory と同じ -atory。

ex.ja: 別のパソコンを買うっていうあなたの計画だけど、問題外よ。

en: In a proud manner.

proudly.ety: From Middle English proutly, proudliche, prudeliche, prudliche, prouteliche, from Old English prūtlīċe, equivalent to proud + -ly.

ex.ja: 「自分で作った」と得意そうに彼は言った。

ex.en: The new Diet member was smoking, leaning back proudly in a chair.
ex.ja: 新代議士はいすにふんぞり返ってたばこをすっていた。

ex.ja: アンチケモナーらはインターネット上で誇らしげにケモナーらに対して異を唱えた。

Of a decimal: having a set of digits that is repeated indefinitely.
A recurrence; a coming round again.

relaxation.ety: Borrowed from Latin relaxatio, relaxationis; equivalent to relax + -ation.

en: An utterance or gesture expressing greeting or honor towards someone, (now especially) a formal, non-verbal gesture made with the arms or…
A kiss, offered in salutation.
To make a gesture in honor of (someone or something).
To act in thanks, honor, or tribute; to thank or extend gratitude; to praise.

salute.ety: Borrowed from Latin salūtō (“to greet; to wish health to”), from salūs (“greeting, good health”), related to salvus (“safe”).

en: The state of being severe.
The degree of something undesirable; badness or seriousness.

severity.ety: From Middle English severity, from Middle French severite (modern French sévérité), from Latin sevēritās. By surface analysis, severe + -ity.

ex.en: He erred on the side of severity.
ex.ja: 彼は厳格すぎた。

ex.ja: 彼が家を飛び出したのは父親が厳しかったせいだ。

Causing shade.

shady.ety: From shade + -y. Compare Saterland Frisian skaadich, skaddich (“shady”), German schattig (“shady”).

ex.ja: ここは、写真を撮るのには暗すぎる。

ex.ja: 叔父の兄の倅が変なビジネスに手を染めて、家名を落とすことになった。

Weak; not holding fast.
Slackly.

slack.ety: From Middle English slak, from Old English slæc (“slack”), from Proto-Germanic *slakaz. For sense of coal dust, compare slag.

Sleek; smooth.
A covering of liquid, particularly oil.
Someone who is clever and untrustworthy.
To make slick.

Akin to Dutch sluik, dialectal Dutch sleek (“even, smooth”), Old Norse slíkr (“sleek, smooth”), Old English slician (“to make sleek, smooth, or glossy”).

note.ja: 中英語 slike（なめらかな）から。「つるつるした」→ 口がなめらか →「口のうまい・巧みな」。

en: A heater, a closed apparatus to burn fuel for the warming of a room.
A device for heating food, (UK) a cooker.
To heat or dry, as in a stove.
To keep warm, in a house or room, by artificial heat.

ex.en: That method's OK but if you use the factor theorem here ...
ex.ja: そのやり方もいいけど、ここは因数定理を使って・・・。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 theōrēma（眺められたもの・命題）から。theory と同じ。「定理」。

en: An area or expanse.
A series of connected body organs, such as the digestive tract.

tract.ety: From Middle English tract, tracte, traht (“a treatise, exposition, commentary”), from Old English traht, tract (“a treatise, exposition, commentary, text, passage”); and also from Middle English tract, tracte (“an expanse of space or time”); both from Latin tractus (“a haul, drawing, a drawing out”), the perfect passive participle of trahō. Doublet of trait.

note.ja: ラテン語 tractus（引くこと・広がり）から。引き伸ばされた広がり →「広い地域・（体の）管・小冊子」。

en: An elected official in Ancient Rome, a tribune of the plebs.
A military officer in Ancient Rome ranking below a legate and above a centurion, a military tribune.

tribune.ety: From Middle English tribune, from Old French tribun, tribune, from Latin tribunus (“tribune, tribal leader”), from tribus (“tribe”).

note.ja: ラテン語 tribunus（部族の長）から。tribe（部族）の代表 →「（古代ローマの）護民官・人民の擁護者」。新聞名にもよく使われる。

en: In an unexpected manner.

ex.en: I was glad that she visited me unexpectedly.
ex.ja: 私は彼女が突然訪ねて来てくれてうれしかった。

ex.en: I ran into him unexpectedly at the airport yesterday.
ex.ja: 僕は昨日空港で偶然彼に会った。

ex.en: I unexpectedly ran into him at the airport yesterday.
ex.ja: 僕は昨日空港で偶然彼に会った。

note.ja: un（否定）+ expected（予期された）+ -ly。ex（外を）+ spectare（見る）。「待ち望んでいなかったのに」→「思いがけなく」。

en: In a direction from lower to higher; toward a higher place; in a course toward the source or origin.
In the upper parts; above.
Directed toward a higher place.

upward.ety: From Old English upweardes, equivalent to up + -ward.

ex.en: The party tickets go for ten dollars and upward.
ex.ja: そのパーティー券は１０ドル以上で売れている。

ex.en: He was looking upward to the sky.
ex.ja: 彼は上をむいて空を見ていた。

ex.en: Prices are on the upward trend.
ex.ja: 物価は上昇傾向にある。

en: A distant view or prospect, especially one seen through some opening, avenue or passage.
A site offering such a view.
To make a vista or landscape of.

vista.ety: Borrowed from Italian vista (“view, sight”), from visto, past participle of vedere (“to see”), from Latin vidēre (“to see”). Compare vision, video, visa.

ex.en: The street, lined with trees, provided a vista of the sea.
ex.ja: 街路樹のある通りの向こうに海が見えた。

ex.en: Researchers announce method of circumventing Windows Vista security features.
ex.ja: Windows Vistaのセキュリティ機能を迂回する方法を研究者が公表します。

note.ja: イタリア語 vista（眺め）から。vis（見る）。→「眺め・展望」。

en: The prevailing fashion or style.
Popularity or a current craze.
To dance in the vogue dance style.
To light a cigarette for (someone).

vogue.ety:
First attested in 1565. Borrowed from Middle French vogue (“wave, course of success”), from Old French vogue, from voguer (“to row, sway, set sail”), from Old Saxon wogōn (“to sway, rock”), var. of wagōn (“to float, fluctuate”), from Proto-Germanic *wagōną (“to sway, fluctuate”) and Proto-Germanic *wēgaz (“water in motion”), from Proto-Germanic *weganą (“to move, carry, weigh”), from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ- (“to move, go, transport”) (compare way).
Akin to Old Saxon wegan (“to move”), Old High German wegan (“to move”), Old English wegan (“to move, carry, weigh”), Old Norse vaga (“to sway, f

ex.en: The French style of dress is in vogue now.
ex.ja: 今、フランス風のドレスが流行している。

ex.en: His novel had a great vogue for a long time.
ex.ja: 彼の小説は長い間たいへん人気があった。

ex.en: This style is much in vogue.
ex.ja: このスタイルは大いにはやっている。

note.ja: フランス語 vogue（波に乗って進むこと）から。voguer（漕ぐ）。「時流に乗ること」→「流行」。

en: Of or pertaining to a volcano or volcanoes.
Produced by a volcano, or, more generally, by igneous agencies.
A volcanic rock.

volcanic.ety: From French volcanique, from volcan (“volcano”); and/or directly from volcan(o) + -ic.

ex.en: Japan is made up of volcanic islands.
ex.ja: 日本は火山列島だ。

ex.en: The surface of the earth rose due to the volcanic activity.
ex.ja: 火山活動で地面が盛り上がった。

ex.en: The volcanic eruption threatened the village.
ex.ja: 火山の爆発がその村をおびやかした。

en: In a wild, uncontrolled manner.
To a ridiculous or extreme degree; extremely.

wildly.ety: From Middle English wildely, wijldeli, wildeliche, equivalent to wild + -ly.

ex.en: Suddenly the horse began to run about wildly.
ex.ja: 馬が急に暴れ出した。

ex.en: Don't run about wildly in the room.
ex.ja: 部屋の中で暴れまわってはいけない。

ex.en: I felt my heart beating wildly.
ex.ja: 私は自分の心臓が激しく打っているのがわかった。

en: Greatly praised or lauded, revered, highly respected.

ex.en: The player was acclaimed by the fans.
ex.ja: その選手はファンに歓呼して迎えられた。

ex.en: He was acclaimed as the best writer of the year.
ex.ja: 彼はその年の最良の作家として褒め称えられた。

ex.en: They acclaimed him as their leader.
ex.ja: 彼らは歓呼して彼を指揮官に迎えた。

note.ja: acclaim（称賛する）+ -ed。ad（〜に）+ clamare（叫ぶ）。「歓声を上げて迎えた」→「称賛された」。claim、exclaim と同じ。

en: To heap up in a mass; to pile up; to collect or bring together (either literally or figuratively), often gradually and without active int…
To gradually grow or increase in quantity or number.

ex.en: He has accumulated quite a collection of books.
ex.ja: 彼は相当数の蔵書を集めた。

ex.en: Dust had accumulated on my desk during my absence.
ex.ja: 私の不在中に埃が机の上に積もっていた。

ex.en: Dust had accumulated on the desk.
ex.ja: 机の上にはほこりがたまっていた。

en: To worship.
To love with one's entire heart and soul; regard with deep respect and affection.

adore.ety: From Middle English *adoren, aouren, from Old French adorer, aorer, from Latin adōrō (“to pray to”), from ad (“to”) + ōrō (“to speak”).

ex.en: The students adore the new English teacher.
ex.ja: 生徒たちはその新しい英語の先生にあこがれている。

ex.en: We have a cat, and we all adore him.
ex.ja: 私たちは猫を飼っています。私たちはみなその猫が好きです。

ex.en: The young professor is adored by the girl students.
ex.ja: その若い教授は女子学生のあこがれの人だ。

note.ja: ad（〜に）+ orare（祈る・話す）。「〜に向かって祈る」→「崇拝する・大好きである」。oral、oracle と同じ or。

en: Of persons, of the same kin; related by blood.
Allied by nature; similar; partaking of the same properties; of the same kind.

akin.ety: From a corruption of of kin, from Middle English of kyn (“related, of kin”), equivalent to a- + kin (1550s). Compare Old English cyn, cynn (“akin, proper, suitable”, adj.).

ex.en: This problem is akin to the one we had last year.
ex.ja: この問題は昨年私達が扱った問題と類似している。

ex.en: Pity is akin to love.
ex.ja: 同情は恋愛に似ている。

ex.en: A buffalo is akin to an ox.
ex.ja: 水牛は牛に似ている。

note.ja: a（〜の）+ kin（親族）。「親族の」→「似ている・同類の」。

A writing system in which letters represent phonemes. (Contrast e.g. logography, a writing system in which each character represents a wo…

ex.en: A is the first letter of the alphabet.
ex.ja: Ａはアルファベットの最初の文字だ。

ex.en: He cannot so much as write the alphabet.
ex.ja: 彼はアルファベットすら書けない。

ex.en: I remember my mother teaching me the alphabet.
ex.ja: 母が私にアルファベットを教えてくれたことを覚えています。

note.ja: ギリシャ文字の最初の2つ alpha + beta から。「アルファベット」。

en: A trainee, especially in a skilled trade.
One who is bound by indentures or by legal agreement to serve a tradesperson, or other person, for a certain time, with a view to learn t…
To put under the care and supervision of a master, for the purpose of instruction in a trade or business.
To be an apprentice to.

apprentice.ety:
From Middle English apprentice, apprentesse, apprentyse, apprentis, from Old French aprentis, plural of aprentif, from Old French aprendre (verb), Late Latin apprendō, from Classical Latin apprehendō.
Compare typologically Latin discipulus (akin to capiō); Russian ухвати́ть (uxvatítʹ), нахвата́ться (naxvatátʹsja), схва́тывать на лету́ (sxvátyvatʹ na letú), and, for another aspect, быть на подхва́те (bytʹ na podxváte) (both akin to хвата́ть (xvatátʹ)).

ex.en: The master carpenter is accompanied by three apprentices.
ex.ja: その棟梁は３人の弟子を従えている。

ex.en: I was Tom's apprentice.
ex.ja: トムの弟子でした。

note.ja: 古フランス語 aprentis（学ぶ人）から。apprendre（学ぶ）、ラテン語 apprehendere（つかむ）。「見習い・徒弟」。

en: A line that is a base for measurement or for construction.
A datum used as the basis for calculation or for comparison.
To provide a baseline for measurement.
To play from the baseline.

note.ja: base（基準）+ line（線）。「基準線・基準」。

ja: 用心する（Beware of the dog：犬に注意）

en: To use caution, pay attention to (used both with and without of).

beware.ety: From Middle English bewar, be war, be ware, forms of Middle English ben ware (“to be on one's guard, be vigilant”, literally “be ware”), equivalent to be + ware or be + aware. Compare Old English bewarian.

ex.en: Beware that you don't get into trouble.
ex.ja: 面倒に巻き込まれないよう注意しなさい。

ex.en: This guy has fast hands so you better beware.
ex.ja: あの男は手が早いから気をつけた方がいいよ。

ex.en: You must beware of strange dogs.
ex.ja: 知らない犬には気をつけなければならない。

note.ja: be + ware（用心深い）。「用心せよ」。aware（気づいている）と同じ ware。

en: A brief, often minimalistic two-piece bathing suit worn by women, especially one that exposes the midriff and navel.
A brief bathing suit covering only the pelvis (equivalent to the bottom portion of a two-piece bikini), worn by any gender.

bikini.ety:
Etymology tree
Marshallese pik
Marshallese ni
Marshallese Pikinnibor.
German Bikinibor.
English Bikinibor.
French Bikini
French bikinibor.
English bikini
From French bikini, named after the place name Bikini, from English Bikini, the name of the atoll where the United States tested nuclear weapons in July 1946; it was reckoned that the bathing suit would cause as much excitement as a nuclear bomb. This name was originally from German Bikini, the colonial name of the atoll as part of German New Guinea, and this was derived from Marshallese Pikinni.

ex.en: Tom was looking at some girls in bikinis.
ex.ja: トムさんはビキニの女の子を見ていた。

ex.en: It seems that bikinis are "in" this year.
ex.ja: 今年はビキニが流行ってるみたいね。

ex.en: Judy decided to wear her new bikini.
ex.ja: ジュディは新しいビキニを着ることにした。

note.ja: 1946年、核実験が行われた太平洋のビキニ環礁の名前から。衝撃的な水着として名づけられた。

en: Sexually attracted to both opposite-sex and same-sex individuals. (Compare pansexual.)
Of flowers: having both pollen and seeds.
A person who is bisexual.
An organism (that is, a species) which has male and female sexes.

bisexual.ety: From bi- + -sexual, via the French bisexuel (bi-, sexuel). Attested since 1792 as a synonym in botany for "hermaphroditic" ("having male and female parts"). First used of sexuality in Richard von Krafft-Ebing's 1886 Psychopathia Sexualis (in German) and Charles Gilbert Chaddock's 1892 English translation thereof, due to the theory that people were naturally attracted to the opposite sex and so the brain or mind of a person attracted to "both" sexes (or to the same sex) must be partly of another sex and thus "hermaphroditic".

ex.en: Tom is either gay or bisexual, I think.
ex.ja: トムは多分ゲイかバイだと思う。

ex.en: Why are Japanese so prejudiced against lesbians and bisexuals?
ex.ja: 日本人はなんでそんなにビアンとかバイとかに偏見を持つのですか？

note.ja: bi（2つの）+ sexual（性の）。「両性愛の」。

en: A broad, well-paved and landscaped thoroughfare.
The landscaping on the sides of a boulevard or other thoroughfare.

boulevard.ety: Borrowed from French boulevard, from Middle French boulevard, bollevart, boulevars, bolevers, bollewerc (“rampart”), from Middle High German bolewerc, bolwerc (modern German Bollwerk) or Middle Dutch bolwerk (“bulwark, bastion”). Doublet of bulwark; more at bole, work.

ex.en: Is this the right bus for Pacific Boulevard?
ex.ja: パシフィック通りに行くには、このバスでいいんでしょうか。

note.ja: フランス語 boulevard（城壁の上の道）から。オランダ語 bolwerk（防塁）。bulwark と同じ語源。城壁跡の広い道 →「大通り」。

en: A band or chain worn around the wrist as jewelry/jewellery or an ornament.
The strap of a wristwatch, used to secure it around the wrist.
To surround with, or as if with, a bracelet; to ring or encompass.

bracelet.ety: From Old French bracelet, diminutive form of bras (“arm”).

ex.en: How many bracelets do you think Mary has?
ex.ja: メアリーって、いくつブレスレットを持ってると思う？

ex.en: This bracelet is more expensive than that one.
ex.ja: このブレスレットはあれよりも高価だ。

ex.en: Tom bought Mary an expensive bracelet.
ex.ja: トムは高価なブレスレットをメアリーに買ってあげた。

note.ja: フランス語 bracel（小さな腕）+ -et。ラテン語 bracchium（腕）。brace と同じ。「腕輪」。

en: A membranous envelope.
A type of simple, dehiscent, dry fruit (seed-case) produced by many species of flowering plants, such as poppy, lily, orchid, willow and …
To form (medicine, etc.) into capsules.
To encapsulate or summarize.

capsule.ety: Borrowed from French capsule, from Latin capsula, diminutive of capsa (“box”).

ex.en: Take this capsule within thirty minutes of each meal.
ex.ja: このカプセルは食後３０分以内に飲んでください。

ex.en: Take two capsules after a meal.
ex.ja: 食後に２カプセル飲みなさい。

ex.en: The medicine was in capsules.
ex.ja: あの薬は、カプセルだったよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 capsula（小箱）から。capsa（箱）+ 縮小。case（箱）と同じ。「カプセル」。

en: One who has been captured or is otherwise confined.
One held prisoner.
Held prisoner; not free; confined.
Subdued by love; charmed; captivated.

captive.ety:
Inherited from Middle English captif; derived from Latin captīvus, probably through a borrowing from a Middle French intermediate. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“seize, hold”).
Doublet of caitiff.

ex.en: He fell captive to her charms.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女の魅力のとりこになった。

note.ja: ラテン語 captivus（捕らえられた）から。capere（取る）。「捕らわれた・捕虜」。capture、captivity と同じ。

en: A written account of events and when they happened, ordered by time.
To record in or as in a chronicle.

chronicle.ety: From Middle English cronicle, cronycle, from Anglo-Norman cronicle, from Old French cronike, from Latin chronica, from Ancient Greek χρονικός (khronikós, “of or concerning time”), from χρόνος (khrónos, “time”).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 chronika（年代の記録）から。chron（時）。→「年代記・記録（する）」。

en: A small evergreen tree native to Sri Lanka and southern India, Cinnamomum verum or Cinnamomum zeylanicum, belonging to the family Lauraceae.
Several related trees, notably the Indonesian cinnamon (Cinnamomum burmanni) and Chinese cinnamon or cassia (Cinnamomum aromaticum or Cin…
Containing cinnamon, or having a cinnamon taste.
Of a yellowish-brown color.

cinnamon.ety: From Middle English synamome, from Old French cinnamone, from Latin cinnamon, cinnamomum, from Ancient Greek κιννάμωμον (kinnámōmon), later κίνναμον (kínnamon), according to Herodotus from Phoenician [Term?], cognate with Hebrew קִנָּמוֹן (qinnāmōn).

ex.en: Try adding a little cinnamon to your coffee.
ex.ja: コーヒーにちょっとだけシナモンを入れてみな。

ex.en: Tom often puts cinnamon in his coffee.
ex.ja: トムはよくコーヒーにシナモンを入れてるよ。

ex.en: Why don't you try putting a little cinnamon in your coffee?
ex.ja: コーヒーにちょっとだけシナモンを入れてみな。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 kinnamōmon から。ヘブライ語・フェニキア語に由来するとされる。

en: To understand or grasp fully and thoroughly; to plumb.

comprehend.ety: From Middle English comprehenden, from Latin comprehendere (“to grasp”), from the prefix com- + prehendere (“to seize”). Doublet of comprend.

ex.en: He could not comprehend the value of her advice.
ex.ja: 彼には彼女の忠告のありがたみが理解できなかった。

ex.en: The professor was unable to comprehend what I meant.
ex.ja: その教授は、私のいわんとすることが理解できなかった。

ex.en: This theory is too difficult for me to comprehend.
ex.ja: この理論はとてもむずかしいので私には理解できない。

note.ja: com（完全に）+ prehend（つかむ）。すっかりつかみ取る →「理解する・含む」。

en: Required; obligatory; mandatory.
Having the power of compulsion; constraining.
Something that is compulsory or required.

compulsory.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin compulsorius, from Latin compulsus. Displaced native Old English ġenīedelīċ.

ex.en: English is a compulsory subject.
ex.ja: 英語は必修科目です。

ex.en: Attendance is compulsory for all members.
ex.ja: 全員出席を義務づけられている。

ex.en: He regards so-called compulsory education as useless.
ex.ja: 彼は、いわゆる義務教育は役に立たない物だと考えている。

note.ja: com（強く）+ puls（押す・駆り立てる）+ ory。強く押しやる →「義務的な・強制的な」。

en: adulterated; impure
made unfit for use by the introduction of unwholesome or undesirable elements.

ex.en: These infections were caused by contaminated milk.
ex.ja: これらの感染病はミルクの汚染が原因だった。

ex.en: A cell phone is as contaminated with bacteria as a toilet is.
ex.ja: 携帯電話と便座は同じくらいの菌に汚染されている。

note.ja: contaminate（汚染する）+ -ed。ラテン語 contaminare（触れて汚す）。con + tangere（触れる）とされる。contact と同じ tang。

en: The act or process of contaminating.
Something which contaminates.

ex.en: People are suffering from the contamination of the water supply.
ex.ja: 人々は水道水の汚染に苦しんでいる。

ex.en: The lake is notorious for its contamination.
ex.ja: その湖は水質汚染で悪名高い。

ex.en: It is essential to prevent salmonella contamination in hen egg production.
ex.ja: 鶏卵生産におけるサルモネラ汚染を防止することが必要です。

note.ja: contaminate + -ion。「汚染」。

en: That which is believed; accepted doctrine, especially religious doctrine; a particular set of beliefs; any summary of principles or opini…
A reading or statement of belief that summarizes the faith it represents; a confession of faith for public use, especially one which is b…
To provide with a creed.

creed.ety:
Inherited from Middle English crede, from Old English crēda, borrowed from Latin crēdō (“to believe”), from Proto-Italic *kresdō, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱréddʰeh₁ti (“to believe, trust”), from earlier *ḱérddʰeh₁ti, from *ḱḗr (“heart”) + *dʰeh₁- (“to place”) + *-ti.
Cognate with Old Irish creitid (“to believe”), Sanskrit श्रद्दधाति (śráddadhāti, “to have faith or faithfulness, to have belief or confidence, believe”).

ex.en: The laws apply to everyone irrespective of race, creed or color.
ex.ja: その法律は人種宗教肌の色に関わらずすべての人に適用される。

note.ja: ラテン語 credo（我は信じる）から。祈りの最初の言葉 →「信条・信念」。credit と同じ cred。

en: Having a consistency which is hard yet brittle, and in a condition to break with a sharp fracture; crumbly, friable, short.
Not limp; firm, stiff; not stale or wilted; fresh; also, effervescent, lively.
In full potato crisp: a thin slice of potato which has been deep-fried until it is brittle and crispy, and eaten when cool; they are typi…
Sometimes with a descriptive word: a crispy, savoury snack made of some other ingredient(s) (such as cornmeal or a vegetable) which is ba…
To make (something) firm yet brittle; specifically (cooking), to give (food) a crispy surface through frying, grilling, or roasting.
To become firm yet brittle; specifically (cooking), of food: to form a crispy surface through frying, grilling, or roasting.

crisp.ety:
The adjective is derived partly from the following:
* Etymology 1, adjective sense 1: Middle English crisp (“curly, wavy”), from Old English crisp (“curly”), from Latin crispus (“of hair: crimped, curly”), possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kris-, from *(s)ker- (“to bend; to turn”).
* Etymology 1, adjective sense 2: from the above, and probably also onomatopoeic, representing a crinkling or crunching sound.
Doublet of crape and crepe.

ex.en: You have a very crisp way of speaking.
ex.ja: あなたの話し方はなかなか歯切れがいいですね。

ex.en: I ate some crisps.
ex.ja: 私はポテトチップスを食べました。

ex.en: These crisps are moreish, aren't they?
ex.ja: このポテチ、やめられなくなるね？

en: A more solid, dense or hard layer on a surface or boundary.
The external, hardened layer of certain foodstuffs, including most types of bread, fried meat, etc.
To cover with a crust.
To form a crust.

From Middle English cruste, from Anglo-Norman and Old French cruste, from Latin crusta (“hard outer covering”), from Proto-Indo-European *krustós (“hardened”), from *krews- (“to form a crust, begin to freeze”), related to Old Norse hroðr (“scurf”), Old English hruse (“earth”), Old High German hrosa (“crust, ice”), Latvian kruvesis (“frozen mud”), Ancient Greek κρύος (krúos, “frost, icy cold”), κρύστα

ex.en: I usually cut the crust off bread.
ex.ja: 普段は、パンの耳はカットしてるよ。

ex.en: I cut the crust off the bread.
ex.ja: パンの耳を切りました。

ex.en: I don't like bread crust.
ex.ja: パンの耳、好きじゃないんだ。

note.ja: ラテン語 crusta（固い外皮）から。「（パンの）皮・外皮・地殻」。crustacean（甲殻類）も同じ。

en: A person or device that cuts (in various senses).
A single-masted, fore-and-aft rigged, sailing vessel with at least two headsails, and a mast set further aft than that of a sloop.

cutter.ety: From Middle English cutter, cuttere, kutter. By surface analysis, cut + -er.

note.ja: cut（切る）+ -er。「切る道具・カッター」。小型の快速船も cutter。

en: A regulated diet that excludes or constrains certain types of food, especially for health reasons; also, a book or similar setting out su…
A prescribed meal plan setting out how the inhabitants of an institution (such as a prison, hospital etc.) should be fed, and on what foods.
Pertaining to a prescribed diet; (generally), relating to what a person or animal eats.
Comprising a food source.

dietary.ety: From Medieval Latin diētārium (“book prescribing diet”), from Latin diaeta (“diet”).

ex.en: Dietary fibre is good for losing weight.
ex.ja: 食物繊維はダイエットに効果的だ。

ex.en: Figs contain dietary fibre.
ex.ja: イチジクには食物繊維が含まれています。

ex.en: Figs contain dietary fiber.
ex.ja: イチジクには食物繊維が含まれています。

note.ja: diet（食事）+ -ary。ギリシャ語 diaita（暮らし方）。「食事の・食生活の」。

en: A formal exposition of a subject, especially a research paper that students write in order to complete the requirements for a doctoral de…
A lengthy lecture on a subject; a treatise; a discourse; a sermon.

ex.en: Have you decided on your dissertation topic?
ex.ja: 卒論のテーマ決まった？

en: Control by means of superior ability, influence, position, or resources; prevailing force.
The exercise of power in ruling; sovereignty; authority; government.

domination.ety: From Middle English domynacion, from Old French dominacion, from Latin dominātiō (“rule, dominion”), from dominor (“domineer; rule”); see dominate.

ex.en: I guess she's into bondage and domination.
ex.ja: 彼女のフェチが緊縛と支配でしょう。

ex.en: They take this negative way of protesting against adult domination.
ex.ja: 大人の支配に対し、彼らはこのような消極的な反抗の仕方をするのである。

note.ja: dom（主人）+ in + ation。主人として支配すること →「支配・優勢」。

en: To eject.
To remove from membership.

expel.ety: Late Middle English: from Latin expellere, from ex- (“out”) + pellere (“to drive”).

ex.en: He expelled the students from the room.
ex.ja: 彼は学生を部屋から出した。

ex.en: I said shut up or I'll have you expelled.
ex.ja: 黙らんと、退学させると言っただろ。

ex.en: Tom was afraid he might be expelled from school.
ex.ja: トムってさ、退学になるんじゃないかってビビってたんだ。

note.ja: ex（外へ）+ pel（押す・駆り立てる）。外へ追い出す →「追放する・除名する」。

en: One of the appendages of a fish, used to propel itself and to manoeuvre/maneuver.
A similar appendage of a cetacean or other marine animal.
To cut the fins from a fish, shark, etc.
(Of a fish) to swim with the dorsal fin above the surface of the water.

fin.ety: From Middle English fin, from Old English finn, from Proto-Germanic *finnō, *finǭ (“dorsal fin”) (compare Dutch vin, German Finne, Swedish finne, fena), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pīn- (“backbone, dorsal fin”) (compare Old Irish ind (“end, point”), Latin pinna (“feather, wing, fin”), Tocharian A spin (“hook”).

note.ja: 古英語 finn から。「ひれ」。

en: Plants considered as a group, especially those of a particular country, region, time, etc.
A book describing the plants of a country, region, time, etc.

note.ja: ローマ神話の花の女神フローラ（Flora）から。ラテン語 flos（花）。flower、flourish と同じ。「植物相」。fauna（動物相）と対。

en: An instance of breaking, a place where something has broken.
A break in bone or cartilage.
To break, or cause something to break.

From Middle English fracture, from Old French fracture, from Latin frāctūra (“a breach, fracture, cleft”), from frangere (“to break”), past participle frāctus, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰreg-, whence also English break. See fraction. Doublet of fraktur.

ex.en: He had an accident and fractured his leg.
ex.ja: 彼は事故にあって脚を骨折した。

ex.en: I fractured my arm.
ex.ja: 腕を骨折しました。

ex.en: The pain of the compound fracture was almost unbearable.
ex.ja: 複雑骨折の痛みはほとんど耐え難かった。

note.ja: fract（壊す）+ ure。壊れたところ →「骨折・割れ目」。

The letter Ɣɣ, used in the alphabets of several African languages, and in lowercase form in the IPA to represent a voiced velar fricative.

gamma.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek γάμμα (gámma). Doublet of gimel.

ex.en: Our sales organization for Gamma is not strong.
ex.ja: ガンマの販売組織が強くありません。

ex.en: Alpha, beta and gamma are Greek letters.
ex.ja: アルファ、ベータ、ガンマはギリシャ文字です。

note.ja: ギリシャ文字の3番目 γ。gamma ray（ガンマ線）。

en: To stare intently or earnestly.
To stare at.
A fixed look; a look of eagerness, wonder, or admiration; a continued look of attention.
In Lacanian psychoanalysis, the relationship of the subject with the desire to look and awareness that one can be viewed.

gaze.ety: From Middle English gasen; akin to Swedish dialectal gasa and Gothic 𐌿𐍃𐌲𐌰𐌹𐍃𐌾𐌰𐌽 (usgaisjan, “to terrify”).

ex.en: Do you know the man gazing at you?
ex.ja: あなたを見つめている男性は知り合いですか。

ex.en: She gazed at me for a long time.
ex.ja: 彼女は長いこと私をじっと見た。

ex.en: I gazed at the sea for hours.
ex.ja: 何時間も海を眺めた。

note.ja: 中英語 gasen から。北欧語に由来するとされる。「じっと見つめる」。

en: The complete genetic information (either DNA or, in some viruses, RNA) of an organism.

genome.ety: From earlier genom, from German Genom, coined by German botanist Hans Winkler in 1920 as a blend of Gen (“gene”) + Chromosom (“chromosome”). By surface analysis, gen(e) + -ome, or a blend of gen(e) + (chromos)ome. Spelling altered to reflect the surface analysis.

note.ja: gene（遺伝子）+ chromosome（染色体）を合わせた語。「生物の遺伝情報の全体」。

en: Small fragments of rock, used for laying on the beds of roads and railways, and as ballast.
A type or grade of small rocks, differentiated by mineral type, size range, or other characteristics.
To apply a layer of gravel to the surface of a road, etc.
To puzzle or annoy.

gravel.ety: From Middle English gravel, grauel, from Old French gravele, diminutive of grave (“gravel, seashore”), from Medieval Latin grava, ultimately from Proto-Celtic *grāwā (“gravel, pebbles”) (compare Breton groa, Cornish grow, Welsh gro), from Proto-Indo-European *gʰroh₁weh₂, from *gʰreh₁w- (“to grind”). Compare also Old English græfa (“coal”).

ex.en: Next year, this gravel road will be paved.
ex.ja: この砂利道は来年舗装されるだろう。

ex.en: We could hear footsteps crunching through the gravel.
ex.ja: 私たちには砂利を踏みしめる足音が聞こえた。

ex.en: We need to bind gravel with cement.
ex.ja: 砂利をセメントで固める必要がある。

note.ja: 古フランス語 gravele（小石）から。grave（砂浜）+ 縮小。「砂利」。

en: The act of cutting of the hair, often done professionally by a barber, hair stylist, or beautician.
The style into which the hair is cut.
To reduce the value assigned to an asset.

ex.en: I could not help laughing at his haircut.
ex.ja: 彼の髪型を見て思わず吹き出してしまった。

ex.en: He gets a haircut three times a month.
ex.ja: 彼は月に３回散髪する。

ex.en: You need not have a haircut this week.
ex.ja: 君は今週は散髪しなくてもよい。

note.ja: hair（髪）+ cut（切ること）。「散髪・髪型」。

en: A high area; land that is higher than surrounding areas.

highland.ety: From Middle English hy laund, holond (“highland, upland”), from Old English hēahland (“highland”), from Proto-West Germanic *hauhaland, *hauhalandī; equivalent to high + land. Cognate with Scots hieland (“highland”), Dutch hoogland (“highland”), German Hochland (“highland”), Danish højland (“highland”), Swedish högland (“highland”).

note.ja: high（高い）+ land（土地）。「高地」。the Highlands はスコットランド北部。

en: To push someone roughly; to crowd; to jostle.
To rush or hurry.
A state of busy activity.
A propensity to work hard and get things done; ability to hustle.

hustle.ety: From Dutch husselen or by metathesis from Dutch hutselen (“to shake up”), a frequentative of hutsen (“to stir, to move something (back and forth)”).

note.ja: オランダ語 hutselen（揺さぶる）から。「押し合う・せかせか動く」→「詐欺」。

en: Not being used appropriately; not occupied; (of time) with no, no important, or not much activity.
Not engaged in any occupation or employment; unemployed; inactive; doing nothing in particular.
To spend (time) in idleness; to waste; to consume.
To lose or spend time doing nothing, or without being employed in business.
The state of idling, of being idle.
The lowest selectable thrust or power setting of an engine.

idle.ety: From Middle English idel, ydel, from Old English īdel, from Proto-West Germanic *īdl, from Proto-Germanic *īdlaz. Cognate with Dutch ijdel (“vain, meaningless”), ijl (“rareified, skinny”), iel (“thin, slender”); German Low German iedel (“vain, idle”); German eitel (“vain, conceited”); and possibly Old Norse illr ("bad"; > English ill).

ex.en: The rain kept the baseball team idle yesterday.
ex.ja: 雨のせいでその野球のチームは昨日試合がなかった。

ex.en: I regret having been idle in my youth.
ex.ja: 私は若い頃怠惰であったことを後悔している。

ex.en: Tom is not an idle boy any longer.
ex.ja: トムはもはや怠惰な少年ではない。

note.ja: 古英語 īdel（むなしい・空の）から。「何もしていない・使われていない」。idol（偶像）とは別語。

en: An official formal accusation for a criminal offence, or the process by which it is brought to a jury.
The official legal document outlining the charges concerned; bill of indictment.

indictment.ety: 18th-century Latinized respelling of Middle English endytement (“action of accusing”), from Anglo-Norman enditement, from enditer, from Late Latin indictāre, from Latin indictus.

ex.en: It is unlikely that this indictment will lead to his deportation.
ex.ja: この告訴を彼の国外退去につながることはおそらくないであろう。

note.ja: in（〜へ）+ dict（言う・宣言する）+ ment。罪を言い渡すこと →「起訴（状）・非難」。発音は［ɪnˈdaɪt-］で c を読まない。

en: Nonstandard; not conforming to rules or expectations.
Of a surface, rough.
A soldier who is not a member of an official military force and who may not use regular army tactics.
One who does not regularly attend a venue.

irregular.ety: From Middle English irreguler, from Old French irreguler, from Medieval Latin or Late Latin irrēgulāris, from in- + regularis, equivalent to ir- + regular.

ex.en: The surface of the moon is irregular.
ex.ja: 月の表面はでこぼこだ。

ex.en: She has a set of irregular teeth.
ex.ja: 彼女は歯並びが悪い。

ex.en: I don't like learning irregular verbs.
ex.ja: 不規則動詞の勉強は好きではない。

note.ja: ir（否定）+ regular（規則的な）。ラテン語 regula（定規・規則）。「不規則な」。

en: Having lots of juice.
Exciting; titillating.

juicy.ety: From Middle English jousy, jowsy (“drunken”, literally “full of juice (liquor)”). By surface analysis, juic(e) + -y.

ex.en: This steak is very juicy.
ex.ja: このステーキ、とてもジューシーね。

ex.en: These figs are juicy.
ex.ja: このイチジク、みずみずしい。

ex.en: I love the taste when I bite into a juicy peach.
ex.ja: みずみずしい桃をかじった時の味が何とも言えません。

note.ja: juice（汁）+ -y。「汁の多い」→ 中身が詰まった →「興味をそそる」。

A vertebrate with three bones in the inner ear and one in the jaw.

ex.ja: それは、人間が哺乳動物であることに由来しています。

ex.ja: 鯨は魚ではなくて、哺乳類です。

ex.en: A bat is not a bird, but a mammal.
ex.ja: 蝙蝠は鳥ではなく哺乳類だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 mamma（乳房）から。「乳で子を育てる動物」→「哺乳類」。

Using a human, as opposed to a computer.

Insignificant; not worthy of importance.

ex.ja: あなたいない人生なんて、虚しいわ。

en: A mistake as to the meaning of something or a specific point of view; erroneous interpretation or comprehension; misconception.
A disagreement; difference of opinion; dissension; quarrel.

misunderstanding.ety: From Middle English mys undirstonding, equivalent to misunderstand + -ing. Compare Dutch misverstand (“misunderstanding”), German Missverständnis (“misunderstanding”), Swedish missförstånd (“misunderstanding”).

ex.en: What he said has brought about a misunderstanding.
ex.ja: 彼の言ったことは誤解を招いた。

ex.en: I think there has been some misunderstanding here.
ex.ja: 何か誤解があったようですが。

ex.en: I don't want there to be any misunderstanding.
ex.ja: どんな誤解もあって欲しくない。

note.ja: mis（誤って）+ understanding（理解）。「誤解」。

en: Given to sudden or frequent changes of mind; temperamental.
Sulky or depressed.

moody.ety: From Middle English mody, modi, from Old English mōdiġ (“brave”), from Proto-Germanic *mōdagaz (“courageous”). By surface analysis, mood + -y.

ex.en: John has been moody since this morning.
ex.ja: ジョンは朝から機嫌が悪かった。

ex.en: I think that Tom is moody.
ex.ja: トムって気分屋だよね。

ex.en: Everyone is entitled to be moody once in a while.
ex.ja: だれもが時には憂うつになる権利を与えられている。

note.ja: mood（気分）+ -y。「気分屋の・不機嫌な」。mood は古英語 mōd（心・勇気）。

en: Redstone circuitry.

ex.en: I ate noodles for the first time today.
ex.ja: 今日初めてつけ麺を食べた。

ex.en: I want to eat Chinese noodles.
ex.ja: ラーメン食べたい。

ex.en: I had a bowl of noodles at a street nearby.
ex.ja: すぐそこでそばを立ち食いしてきた。

note.ja: ドイツ語 Nudel から。「麺」。

en: A shrine dedicated to some prophetic deity.
A person such as a priest through whom the deity is supposed to respond with prophecies or advice.

oracle.ety: From Middle English oracle, from Old French oracle m, from Latin ōrāculum n.

ex.en: The oracle was fulfilled.
ex.ja: 神託は実現した。

note.ja: ラテン語 oraculum（神のお告げ）から。orare（話す・祈る）。「神託・賢人」。adore と同じ or。

en: To extend over and partly cover something.
To co-occur, to happen at the same time.
Something that overlaps or is overlapped.
a situation in the game where an attacking line has more players in it than the defensive line coming to meet it. The attacking side may …

overlap.ety:
From over- + lap.
Cognate with Dutch overlap.

ex.en: When inserting the budwood into the root stock, make the cambium layers overlap.
ex.ja: 穂木を台木に差し込む際、形成層を重ね合わせるようにします。

note.ja: over（上に）+ lap（重ねる）。「上に重なる」→「重複」。

en: To look slyly, or with the eyes half closed, or through a crevice; to peep.
To be only slightly, partially visible, as if peering out from a hiding place.
A quick glance or look.

peek.ety: From Middle English *peken, piken, pyken (“to peep”), probably a fusion of Middle English pepen (“to peep”) and keken, kiken (“to keek, look, spy”), equivalent to a blend of peep + keek. Perhaps also possibly a metathetic alteration of Middle English kepen, kipen, kypen (“to keep, look, observe, watch”).

ex.en: Tom opened the box and peeked inside.
ex.ja: トムは箱を開け、中をのぞき込んだ。

ex.en: I promise not to peek.
ex.ja: のぞき見しないって約束するよ。

ex.en: You can see the sun peeking through the clouds.
ex.ja: 雲の切れ間から太陽が見えます。

note.ja: 中英語 piken から。語源ははっきりしない。「のぞき見る」。peek-a-boo（いないいないばあ）。

en: A polygon with five sides and five angles.
A fort with five bastions.

pentagon.ety: From Middle French pentagone, from Late Latin pentagōnum, from Ancient Greek πεντάγωνον (pentágōnon), noun use of the neuter of the adjective πεντάγωνος (pentágōnos, “five-angled”), from πέντε (pénte, “five”) + -γωνος (-gōnos, “angled”). Equivalent to penta- + -gon.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 pente（5）+ gōnia（角）。「五角形」→ 五角形の建物の米国防総省。

en: A car of this brand, reputably high-performance and expensive.

Porsche.ety:
Borrowed from German Porsche
* (automotive): From the surname of the founder, Ferdinand Porsche, beginning 1931.

ex.en: They say that Tom has a Porsche.
ex.ja: トムってポルシェに乗ってるんだって。

ex.en: The careless IT manager died by getting run over with his own Porsche.
ex.ja: おっちょこちょいなIT社長は自分のポルシェに轢かれ死亡しました。

ex.en: He has two cars; one is a Benz and the other is a Porsche.
ex.ja: 彼は車を２台持っていて、１台はベンツで、もう１台はポルシェだ。

en: Fired ceramic wares that contain clay when formed.
A potter's shop or workshop, where pottery is made.

pottery.ety: From Old French poterie, from potier (“potter”), from the root of pot, equivalent to pot + -ery. First attested in the 13th century.

ex.en: The pottery was baked by fire.
ex.ja: 陶器は火で焼かれた。

ex.en: Saturday is the pottery class I've been attending since last year.
ex.ja: 土曜日、去年から通い始めた陶芸教室。

ex.en: Clay is the essential ingredient in making pottery.
ex.ja: 泥は陶器を作るのに必要な材料です。

en: An extensive area of relatively flat grassland with few, if any, trees, especially in North America.

prairie.ety: Borrowed from French prairie, from Old French praerie, from Vulgar Latin *prataria, from Latin prātum (“meadow”) + -aria.

ex.en: Nothing but grass was to be seen in the prairie.
ex.ja: 大草原では草以外何も見えなかった。

ex.en: Trees do not grow on prairies.
ex.ja: 大草原には木が生えない。

ex.en: Laura Ingalls grew up on the prairie.
ex.ja: ローラ・インガルスは、大草原で育った。

note.ja: フランス語 prairie（牧草地）から。ラテン語 pratum（草地）。「大草原」。

en: A practical joke or mischievous trick.
To perform a practical joke on; to trick and make a fool of someone.
To make a prank call to (someone).

prank.ety: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from Middle English pranken (“to adorn, arrange one's attire”), probably from Middle Dutch pronken, proncken (“to flaunt, make a show, arrange one's attire”), related to German prangen (“to make a show, be resplendent”), Dutch prangen (“to squeeze, press”), Danish pragt (“pomp, splendor”), all from Proto-Germanic *pranganą, *prangijaną, *prag- (“to press, squeeze, thring”), from Proto-Indo-European *brengʰ- (“to press, squeeze”). Or, perhaps ultimately related to Proto-Germanic *brahtaz, similar to Dutch pracht (“splendor”), Swedish prakt (“glory, pomp”) (loaned from

ex.en: At first I thought it was a prank.
ex.ja: 最初、いたずらかと思った。

ex.en: Tom and Mary were making prank phone calls.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは、いたずら電話をかけていた。

ex.en: Stop playing pranks on me!
ex.ja: 悪ふざけもほどほどにしてほしいな。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。16世紀から「いたずら・悪ふざけ」。

en: Occurring before a state of readiness or maturity has arrived.
Taking place earlier than anticipated, prepared for, or desired.
An infant born prematurely.

premature.ety: From Latin praemātūrus, equivalent to pre- + mature. First use appears c. 1440 in a translation of Palladius's De Re Rustica.

ex.en: He made a premature decision on the matter.
ex.ja: 彼はその件について早まった決定をした。

ex.en: It is premature to discuss it now.
ex.ja: それを今論議するのはまだ早い。

ex.en: It is premature to put the plan into practice now.
ex.ja: 今その計画を実施するのは、時期尚早である。

zh: 精神病醫生 /精神病医生

ex.en: A blonde is speaking to her psychiatrist.
ex.ja: 金髪女性が精神科医と会話をしている。

en: The most abundant mineral on the earth's surface, of chemical composition silicon dioxide, SiO₂. It occurs in a variety of forms, both cr…

quartz.ety: From German Quarz, from Middle High German (Central East German) quarz, twarc, from a West Slavic language [compare Polish twardy (“hard”), Czech tvrdý (“hard”)], from Proto-Slavic *tvьrdъ ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *twerH- (“to enclose, grab”).

note.ja: ドイツ語 Quarz から。語源ははっきりしない。「石英・水晶」。

en: The condition of being a resident of a particular place.
The home or residence of a person, especially in the colonies.

ex.en: I don't have permanent residency.
ex.ja: 永住権はありません。

ex.en: What's the difference between permanent residency status and naturalization?
ex.ja: 永住権と帰化って、どう違うの？

en: Answering, replying or responding
Able to receive and respond to external stimuli.

responsive.ety: From Middle French responsif, from Late Latin responsivus.

en: To make a loud, deep cry, especially from pain, anger, or other strong emotion.
To laugh in a particularly loud manner.
A long, loud, deep shout, as of rage or laughter, made with the mouth wide open.
The cry of the lion.

roar.ety:
From Middle English roren, raren, from Old English rārian (“to roar; wail; lament”), from Proto-West Germanic *rairōn, from Proto-Germanic *rairōną (“to bellow; roar”), from Proto-Indo-European *rey- (“to shout; bellow; yell; bark”), perhaps of imitative origin.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian roorje (“to roar”), German röhren (“to roar”).

ex.en: The commander was roaring at his soldiers.
ex.ja: 隊長は兵士を怒鳴りつけていた。

ex.en: The cold north wind was roaring outside.
ex.ja: 外では冷たい北風が轟々と吹き荒れていた。

ex.en: Father roared at me in anger.
ex.ja: 父はわたしを怒ってどなった。

note.ja: 古英語 rārian（ほえる）から。擬音的な語。「ほえる・とどろく」。

en: To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.
To decline in function or utility.
The process of becoming rotten; putrefaction.
Decaying matter.

rot.ety: Inherited from Middle English roten, rotten, from Old English rotian (“to rot, become corrupted, ulcerate, putrefy”), from Proto-West Germanic *rotēn, from Proto-Germanic *rutāną (“to rot”).

ex.en: Fruit tends to rot right away.
ex.ja: 果物はすぐにくさりがちである。

ex.en: It was discarded because it rotted.
ex.ja: 腐ってたから捨てたよ。

ex.en: Put the meat in the refrigerator, or it will rot.
ex.ja: 肉を冷蔵庫に入れなさい。さもないと腐るよ。

note.ja: 古英語 rotian（腐る）から。rotten と同じ。

en: A musician who composes songs; especially writing the song's lyrics and/or creating a melody or a tune for the song.
A long stick with a sharp tip used as a weapon for throwing or thrusting, or anything used to make a thrusting motion.
A soldier armed with such a weapon; a spearman.
To pierce with a spear.
To penetrate or strike with, or as if with, any long narrow object; to make a thrusting motion that catches an object on the tip of a lon…
Male.
Pertaining to male family members.

spear.ety:
From Middle English spere, sperre, spear, from Old English spere, from Proto-West Germanic *speru, from Proto-Germanic *speru, from Proto-Indo-European *sperH-.
Cognates
See also West Frisian spear, Dutch speer, German Speer, Old Norse spjǫr, *sparrô, Middle Dutch sparre (“rafter”), Old Norse sparri (“spar, rafter”), sperra (“rafter, beam”); also Latin sparus (“short spear”), Albanian ferrë (“thorn, thornbush”).

ex.en: Whether rain or spears fall, I will go.
ex.ja: 雨が降ろうが槍が降ろうが、俺は行く。

ex.en: Whether rain or spears shall fall, I will go.
ex.ja: 雨が降ろうが槍が降ろうが、俺は行く。

ex.en: Whether rain shall fall, whether spears shall fall, I will go.
ex.ja: 雨が降ろうが槍が降ろうが、俺は行く。

note.ja: 古英語 spere（槍）から。spar（円材）と同系。

en: A pushing or goading toward action.
Any action or condition that creates a response; sensory input.

ex.en: Just as the body needs exercise, so the mind needs stimulation to stay healthy.
ex.ja: 身体が運動を必要とするように、精神も健康であるために刺激を必要とする。

ex.en: Nothing I do brings me stimulation, so keeping up my motivation is really tough.
ex.ja: 何事もやってるうちに刺激がなくなってくるので、モチベーションを保つのはなかなか大変だ。

note.ja: stimulate（刺激する）+ -ion。ラテン語 stimulus（牛を追う突き棒）。「刺激」。

en: Abandoned or marooned.
Run aground on a shore or reef.

Having elegance or taste or refinement in manners or dress.

ex.en: This is not very stylish.
ex.ja: これはあまりおしゃれじゃない。

note.ja: style（様式）+ -ish。ラテン語 stilus（尖筆）。「書き方」→「様式」→「おしゃれな」。

ex.ja: 発展途上国では優れた技術者が不足している。

note.ja: technic（技術）+ -ian。ギリシャ語 technē（技術）。「技術者」。technology と同じ tech。

ex.ja: 彼らは津波の危険を知らされていなかった。

ex.ja: 津波警報は解除された。

en: Something which has been transcribed; a writing or composition consisting of the same words as the original; a written copy.
A copy of any kind; an imitation.

ex.en: We used the transcripts of the recordings of telephone conversations.
ex.ja: 電話での会話の録音を文学化した資料を用いた。

note.ja: tran（向こうへ）+ script（書かれた）。別の紙に書き写したもの →「写し・記録・成績証明書」。

en: A long, narrow ditch or hole in the ground; either manmade, or formed naturally through erosion or tectonic plate movement.
A narrow excavation as used in warfare, as a cover for besieging or emplaced forces.
To invade, especially with regard to the rights or the exclusive authority of another; to encroach.
To excavate an elongated pit for protection of soldiers and or equipment, usually perpendicular to the line of sight toward the enemy.

trench.ety: Borrowed into Middle English from Old French trenche. Doublet of tranche and traunch. Possible doublet of English: truncate

ex.en: Tom was wearing a trench coat.
ex.ja: トムはトレンチコートを着ていた。

ex.en: After we finish digging the trench, planting the flowers will be easy.
ex.ja: 溝を掘り終えたら花を植えるのは簡単だよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 trenche（切ること・溝）から。trancher（切る）。「溝・塹壕」。第一次大戦の塹壕で着たコート →「トレンチコート」。

en: An article of clothing that covers the part of the body between the waist and the ankles or knees, and is divided into a separate part fo…

ex.en: He was wearing black trousers and a beautiful white shirt.
ex.ja: 彼は黒いズボンをはき、美しい白いワイシャツを着ていました。

note.ja: スコットランド・ゲール語 triubhas（ぴったりしたズボン）から。

From un- + willing.

ex.en: She was unwilling to tell her name.
ex.ja: 彼女は名前を言うのを嫌がった。

ex.en: I am unwilling to study now.
ex.ja: 今は勉強したくない。

ex.en: He was unwilling to go.
ex.ja: 彼は行きたくなかった。

note.ja: un（否定）+ willing（進んで〜する）。「気が進まない」。will（意志）と同じ。

en: The state of being valid, authentic or genuine.
State of having legal force.

validity.ety: From valid + -ity, borrowed from Middle French validité, from Late Latin validitas.

en: The act or process of verifying.
The state of being verified.

verification.ety: From Middle French verification (modern French vérification) or its etymon Medieval Latin vērificātiō. By surface analysis, verificate + -ion.

ex.en: Please activate your new password via email verification.
ex.ja: 新パスワードはメール認証で有効化してください。

en: A solemn promise to perform some act, or behave in a specified manner, especially a promise to live and act in accordance with the rules …
A declaration or assertion.
To make a vow; to promise.
To make a vow regarding (something).

vow.ety: Inherited from Middle English vowe, voue, that from Old French vut, in turn from Latin vōtum (“a promise, dedication, vow”), from vovēre (“to promise, vow”). Not related to avow. Doublet of vote.

ex.en: He vowed to give up smoking.
ex.ja: 彼は禁煙を心に誓った。

ex.en: I vowed that I would never speak to her again.
ex.ja: 彼女には二度と話しかけないと誓った。

ex.en: I vowed that I would never speak to Tom again.
ex.ja: 二度とトムには話しかけないと誓った。

note.ja: ラテン語 votum（誓い・願い）から。vote と同じ語源。「誓い・誓う」。

en: The state of being vulnerable; susceptibility to attack or injury, either physical or emotional; the state or condition of being weak or …
A specific weakness in the protections or defences that (literally or figuratively) surround someone or something.

note.ja: vulnerable（傷つきやすい）+ -ity。ラテン語 vulnus（傷）。「傷つきやすさ・脆弱性」。

en: Which ever; emphatic form of 'which'.
Regardless of the ... that; no matter which.
Which ever; emphatic form of 'which'.
Irrespective of the one(s) that; no matter which one(s).

whichever.ety: From whiche ever, whiche evere, which ever, which evere; equivalent to which + -ever.

ex.en: Choose whichever of them is becoming to you.
ex.ja: その中でどれでも一番あなたに似合っているものを選んでください。

ex.en: You can use whichever pen I'm not using.
ex.ja: 私の使っていないペンならどれでも使って良いよ。

ex.en: Whichever you read, you will find it interesting.
ex.ja: どちらを読んでもおもしろいだろう。

en: Great anger; (countable) an instance of this.
Punishment, retribution, or vengeance resulting from anger; (countable) an instance of this.

wrath.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English wratthe (“anger, hostility, distress retribution”) [and other forms], from Old English wrǣþþu (“ire, wrath”) [and other forms], from Proto-West Germanic *wraiþiþu (“anger, fury, wrath”), from *wraiþ (“angry, furious, wroth; hostile, violent; bent, twisted”) (from Proto-Germanic *wraiþaz (“angry, furious, wroth; hostile, violent; bent, twisted”), from Proto-Indo-European *wreyt- (“to twist”)) + *-iþu (suffix forming abstract nouns). Effectively analysable as wroth + -th (abstract nominal suffix); compare Dutch wreedte.
The verb is derived from Middle Engl

ex.en: They called down the wrath of God upon the heads of their enemies.
ex.ja: 彼らは敵の上に天罰が下ることを祈った。

ex.en: A soft answer turneth away wrath.
ex.ja: 柔和な答は怒りをしりぞける。

ex.en: My wrath shall far exceed the love I ever bore.
ex.ja: 私の怒りは私がいだき続けた愛を遥かに上回るだろう。

note.ja: 古英語 wrǣththu（怒り）から。wroth（怒った）、writhe（身もだえする）と同系。

en: The basic unit of money in China.

yuan.ety: From Mandarin 元 (yuán), from 圓／圆 (yuán, “circle > round coin”) referring to the piece of eight. Compare Japanese 円(えん) (en), Korean 원(圓) (won). Doublet of yen and won.

note.ja: 中国語「元（圓）」から。「丸い硬貨」の意。日本の円（yen）と同じ漢字の語。

en: Synonym of enlightenment, particularly the kind acquired through Zen meditation.
An approach to instruction, understanding, or an activity similarly emphasizing simplicity and intuition rather than conventional thinkin…
Wise, displaying enlightenment or similar wisdom, insightful, unburdened and free of worries, extremely relaxed and capable.

zen.ety: From Zen. In more general use, popularized by Eugen Herrigel's 1948 Zen in the Art of Archery and Robert M. Pirsig's 1974 Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance.

ex.en: They say that Zen strengthens our mind.
ex.ja: 禅は私たちの心を鍛練するといわれる。

ex.en: They say Zen cultivates our mind.
ex.ja: 禅は私たちの心を鍛練するといわれる。

ex.en: He sat in Zen meditation.
ex.ja: 彼は座禅を組んだ。

note.ja: 日本語「禅」から。中国語 chan、サンスクリット語 dhyāna（瞑想）にさかのぼる。

en: An assistant.
An officer who acts as assistant to a more senior one; an aide-de-camp.

aide.ety: Borrowed from French aide ("aid; assistant", as in aide-de-camp (“field assistant”)). More at aid.

ex.en: The aide suggested a change in tactics to him.
ex.ja: 副官は戦術の変更を彼に提案した。

ex.en: The dictator had the absolute loyalty of all his aides.
ex.ja: その独裁者は側近たち全員の絶対的な忠誠を受けた。

en: Loyalty or commitment to a cause, group, nation or of a subordinate to a superior.

allegiance.ety: From Middle English alegiaunce, from Anglo-Norman alegaunce (“loyalty of a liege-servant to one's lord”), variant of Old French ligeance, from lige (“vassal, liegeman”). More at liege.

ex.en: The knight swore an oath of allegiance to the king.
ex.ja: 騎士が王への忠誠を誓った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 ligeance（臣下の務め）から。liege（主君）。「忠誠」。

en: Suitable; appropriate; fit or fitted; suited.
Having a habitual tendency; habitually liable or likely; disposed towards.

apt.ety: From Old French apte, from Latin aptus (“suitable, fitting”). Either from obsolete apere (“to fasten, to join, to fit”), akin to apisci (“to reach, attain”) (compare with Greek ἅπτειν (áptein, “to fasten”) and Sanskrit आप्त (āpta, “fit”), from आप् (āp, “to reach, attain”)) or from *h₂ep- (“to join, fit (in)”).

ex.en: We are apt to speak ill of others.
ex.ja: 私達は他人の悪口を言いがちだ。

ex.en: We are apt to forget this fact.
ex.ja: 私達はこのことを忘れがちである。

ex.en: He is apt to forget people's name.
ex.ja: 彼は人の名前を忘れやすい。

note.ja: ラテン語 aptus（結びつけられた・ふさわしい）から。「適切な・〜しがちな」。adapt、aptitude と同じ。

en: An incarnation of a deity, particularly Vishnu.
One which serves to act in place of or on behalf of the entity; a simulacrum.

avatar.ety:

en: Characterized by the presence of moisture; not dry; slightly wet; damp.
Of eyes: wet with tears; tearful; also (obsolete), watery due to some illness or to old age.

To rain lightly; to drizzle.

moist.ety:
The adjective is derived from Middle English moist, moiste [and other forms], from Anglo-Norman moist, moiste, moste, Middle French moiste, and Old French moiste, muste (“damp, moist, wet”) (modern French moite); further etymology uncertain, perhaps a blend of a Late Latin variant of Latin mūcidus (“mouldy, musty”) + a Late Latin derivative of Latin mustum (“unfermented or partially fermented grape juice or wine, must”).
The noun is derived from the adjective.

ex.en: The air is soft, the soil moist.
ex.ja: 空気は穏やかで、土には湿り気がある。

ex.en: Her eyes were moist with tears.
ex.ja: 彼女の目は涙で濡れていた。

ex.en: It's something black, sweet, and moist.
ex.ja: 黒くて、甘くて、しっとりした何かです。

note.ja: 古フランス語 moiste（湿った）から。moisture と同じ。

en: The ruler of an absolute monarchy or the head of state of a constitutional monarchy.

monarch.ety:

* (butterfly): See monarch butterfly.

ex.ja: 君主はその葬儀に出席することになっている。

mustard.ety: From Middle English mustard, from Old French moustarde (French moutarde), from moust (“must”), from Latin mustum. Doublet of mostarda.

en: Any of various deciduous trees or shrubs in the genus Salix, in the willow family Salicaceae, found primarily on moist soils in cooler zo…
